check.title: Rival blocs before 1914
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
check.referenceAnswer: They divided Europe into rival blocs, increasing suspicion and making a local crisis more likely to spread.
check.feedback: The alliances mattered because they turned tension into competing blocs, not because they directly caused one specific battle.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum and the widening war.

check.title: From assassination to ultimatum
check.prompt: What happened after the Sarajevo assassination that helped widen the conflict?
check.referenceAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, and the dispute expanded into a broader war through alliance commitments.
check.feedback: The key link is the ultimatum and escalation, not the assassination alone.

check.feedback: Remember the war starts in 1914 and ends in 1918, not the other way around.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: Rival blocs before 1914
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: Rival blocs before 1914
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival blocs, increasing suspicion and making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances mattered because they turned tension into competing blocs, not because they directly caused one specific battle.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: From assassination to ultimatum
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum and the widening war.
1914 began the war, and 1918 ended it with the Armistice.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: From assassination to ultimatum
activities.body: What happened after the Sarajevo assassination that helped widen the conflict?
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum and the widening war.
activities.correctAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, and the dispute expanded into a broader war through alliance commitments.
activities.feedback: The key link is the ultimatum and escalation, not the assassination alone.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: 1914 to 1918 timeline
activities.body: What is the basic chronology from 1914 to 1918?
activities.concept: 1914 began the war, and 1918 ended it with the Armistice.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the Armistice.
activities.feedback: Remember the war starts in 1914 and ends in 1918, not the other way around.

activities.label: Repair
activities.title: Repair the first explanation
activities.body: Compare the first explanation with this verified reference: They divided Europe into rival blocs, increasing suspicion and making a local crisis more likely to spread. Correct the exposed relationship in your own words without copying the reference.
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival blocs, increasing suspicion and making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances mattered because they turned tension into competing blocs, not because they directly caused one specific battle.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Explain the corrected relationship again
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914? Explain it again after the repair without copying the model or reference answer.
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival blocs, increasing suspicion and making a local crisis more likely to spread.
activities.feedback: The alliances mattered because they turned tension into competing blocs, not because they directly caused one specific battle.

activities.label: Recall check
activities.title: War start and end
activities.body: Which statement correctly gives the basic chronology of World War I?
activities.concept: Recognition transfer: 1914 began the war, and 1918 ended it with the Armistice.
choices: It began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
It began in 1918 and ended in 1914.
It began with the Sarajevo assassination in 1918.
It ended before the Sarajevo assassination in 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: It began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
activities.feedback: The correct timeline starts in 1914 and ends in 1918.
